## TL;DR

A phone now has exactly one task detail: the shared `TaskDrawer`, mounted once by `App.vue` for every entry point. The read-only `MobileTaskDetail` stub and its test are gone. Below 720px the drawer becomes a full-screen phone page with labelled 44×44 Back and close controls, a scrollable seven-tab strip, 44px controls, 16px inputs and a Paused state with **Resume work**. Queue cards, Search, notices, `?task=<id>&tab=…` deep links and post-create all converge on it. I also stabilised the remote-runner `agent-serve-guard` test and extended the WebKit smoke to assert phone geometry at 360px.

## Work and rationale

The bug was structural. `App.vue` hid `TaskDrawer` whenever a narrow `/work?task=` route was active and `WorkView` rendered `MobileTaskDetail` instead. That stub had no review report, PM chat, Changes/Dev/Debug tabs, edit fields or most actions, so a task told different stories depending on where it was opened. Patching the stub to parity would have preserved two state machines and guaranteed future drift, so I made the drawer's phone mode the single detail.

`WorkView`'s narrow branch now owns only the queue; it keeps the queue mounted with `v-show` so Back is instant and local filter/sort state survives. `App.vue` always mounts `TaskDrawer` and hides the bottom `MobileTabs` only while a task is open. The `?task=` watcher still opens the drawer and applies `?tab=` after `open()` sets the status default, so `/work?task=1128&tab=changes` lands on Changes rather than Review.

Route ownership needed care. On desktop the drawer opens and immediately clears `?task=`; on a phone that param is the detail-page address and must stay so browser Back returns to the queue and re-shows it. Because the drawer is global, every close path (X, Escape, overlay, an action that calls `ui.close()`) now drops `task` and `tab` through a watcher on open state, not just the dialog's dismiss event. The phone Back control replaces `/work` when the drawer was opened there and pushes `/work` when it came from another page such as Search. WorkView's task-param watcher closes the drawer when the param disappears, so browser Back stays in sync.

Pause was the one state the drawer did not model explicitly. `repo.pauseWork` records the task in `pausedIds` immediately, but `runningIds` may still contain it until the process exits, and the status card ignored `isPaused`. I added a `workPaused` key above `workRunning` in the shared status priority (excluding PM activity). The status line reads “Paused”, the header chip follows, the Pause button disappears as soon as the POST returns, and the primary action becomes **Resume work**, disabled only while the old process is still running. `pausedIds` is seeded from `/api/agents/running`, so the state survives a reload.

I also surfaced the card's Acknowledge actions in the drawer quickbar for fresh-done and AI-created tasks, which otherwise had no phone path. Hold/Release hold, Review again, archive and editable metadata were already there.

The phone chrome is CSS-only below 720px. The drawer fills `100vw`; the header's title column shrinks (`min-width: 0`) so long chips cannot push the close off-screen; Back and close are 44×44 with accessible names; tabs, quickbar, review/save/delete, the agent picker and canned prompts meet the 44px floor; and inputs/textareas are 16px so iOS Safari does not zoom. The drawer uses `overflow-x: clip`, not `hidden`: `hidden` still creates a scroll container that focus/`scrollIntoView` can shift, taking the close with it.

The queued handoff failure was unrelated to the feature. `agent-serve-guard.test.ts`'s real-process check now uses a minimal explicit environment, writes both streams to file descriptors, handles spawn errors, and fails on its own 20s deadline with the captured output. The remote runner still occasionally saw a non-zero exit with empty stderr — a killed child, not a guard regression — so the test retries a signal or empty-stderr non-zero up to three times, fails a timeout immediately (a regression leaves the server bound), and reports exit code, signal, attempts and stdout.

The smoke measurement was also hardened: it waits for the drawer's 280ms slide-in transform to settle, targets a dedicated `data-test-id="task-detail-close"` (asserting exactly one match), and includes measured rectangles, scroll offsets and inner width in any failure. That removed a mid-animation race and made remote failures name the exact geometry.

## Approaches tried

Growing `MobileTaskDetail` to parity was rejected: it would duplicate the drawer's status priority, review/report rendering, PM/Dev sessions, diff viewer and edit flow. Replacing the stub inside `WorkView` was also rejected because Search, notices and new-task open `ui.active` without a Work route; only a single mount above the router makes every entry point identical.

For the tab strip I used the existing `drawer-tabs-scroll` opt-in class rather than making `.drawer-tabs` scroll globally. The story panel already uses it and the shared base rule preserves the input panel's shrink-to-fit behaviour; applying it only when narrow keeps desktop unchanged.

For paused state I rejected deriving it from “not running”: that is wrong while an agent is still exiting and cannot distinguish a pause from a crash. The explicit `pausedIds` signal gives immediate, honest feedback.

For verification I extended the existing WebKit smoke. It opens `/work?task=9001&tab=changes` at 360px and checks body overflow, 44×44 labelled Back/close, the selected Changes tab, last-tab reachability after scrolling, a 16px composer and 44px canned prompts/agent picker. Component tests cover entry-point parity, deep-link tab selection, close-clears-route, Paused/Resume and a failed reviewer keeping **Review again** reachable.

## Challenges and blockers

The subtlety was the two route models: `?task=` is transient control state on desktop but a page address on a phone. Clearing it in the wrong place either re-opens the drawer after a dismiss or leaves a stale task URL. The solution keeps desktop's clear-on-open behaviour and gives the phone an explicit close-and-clear path on every close route while preserving Back.

A second subtlety was CSS specificity: the status card and done-error use scoped rules that outrank a global selector. Their 22px gutter already fits 360px, so I deleted the intended overrides rather than escalating with `!important`.

I have no physical phone. Verification is headless WebKit against the built app at 360px and 390px (geometry, overflow, tab reachability, composer font size) plus jsdom component tests at 360/390/412. The 16px rule prevents the reported iOS zoom, but “no zoom on a real iPhone” was not observed; sibling #1139 carries the physical-device pass.

## Key learnings

One detail component is the only durable fix for entry-point parity. A second mobile stub creates two state machines and guaranteed disagreement.

A route param can be either transient UI state or a page address depending on layout. The detail owner must clear that address on every close path, not just its dismiss event.

An explicit `pausedIds` signal beats inferring a pause from a stopped process; keep its action disabled until the old process exits.

Flakiness on a shared runner is usually isolation or an environmental kill, not the behaviour under test. Capture every stream and exit signal, fail on your own deadline, and retry only the environmental failure — never a regression's timeout.
